extracted.intended_audience: small biotech / small business applicants preparing NIH NIAID SBIR (R43/R44) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: A Phase I SBIR (R43) application sample for an NIAID-funded small business vaccine project; includes required application components, compliance sections, experimental plans, facilities, budgets, and personnel biosketches. Useful as a template for preparing similar NIH SBIR proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to FOA/application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the specific FOA for current formatting and submission rules; use NIAID sample applications as a guide but verify updates on the FOA webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) and Required Face Page Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the SF 424 (R&R) face page information: type of submission, federal identifier, organizational DUNS, legal name, applicant contact, EIN/TIN, type of applicant, project title, start and end dates, congressional district, and certification/signature of authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all mandatory fields are completed accurately; include DUNS, EIN, performance site locations, and authorized representative signature/date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise project summary/abstract describing objectives, general approach, expected outcomes and significance (page labeled 'ABSTRACT / SUMMARY').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the aims, approach, and expected impact in the abstract so reviewers can quickly grasp the project; include key methods and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance Statement (Narrative Attachment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief narrative (public health relevance) explaining how the proposed work will impact public health (e.g., development of a broadly protective influenza vaccine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about population-level impact, translational relevance, and potential public health benefits in non-technical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Structure (Introduction, Specific Aims, Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an Introduction, Specific Aims page, and Research Strategy (approach, preliminary data, significance, innovation, potential problems/alternatives, timelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PHS 398 conventions: succinct Specific Aims, clear Significance/Innovation statements, detailed Approach with experimental design, contingency plans, and milestones/ timelines (Activities & Milestones chart).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional and company facilities, laboratory space, equipment, administrative resources and access to core facilities (including square footage and biosafety features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail to show capability to perform the work (e.g., BSL2+ tissue culture room, HEPA filtration, list of major instruments, access to libraries and shared facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: cGMP Production and Regulatory Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing production for clinical testing, describe planned cGMP production space and compliance with FDA guidance ('CGMP for Phase 1 Investigational Drugs' under regulation 21 CFR 201.2(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State timeline and size of pilot plant, and commitment to meet FDA cGMP requirements for Phase I material production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory Quality Assurance Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a fully developed laboratory Quality Assurance Plan to generate defensible data meeting quality objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe QA procedures, data management, SOPs, and any QA experience participating in government contract bids or regulated work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches for senior/key personnel following the required format; 'DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.' Include Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Education/Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant experience that demonstrates ability to carry out the project; adhere strictly to page limits and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Personnel Roles and Collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: List Senior/Key Persons, their project roles (PD/PI, Co-Investigator, Collaborator), organizational affiliations, and attach biographical sketches and current & pending support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify responsibilities, named collaborators (e.g., Baylor College of Medicine co-investigator, CDC collaborator), and any subaward/consortium arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Research & Related budgets for each budget period and cumulative budget, including budget justification and any consortium/subaward budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize direct costs, justify personnel effort, supplies, animal costs, subcontractor expenses; ensure budgets align with FOA limits and SBIR guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Sites and Project/Performance Site Location(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: List primary and additional performance sites with full addresses and congressional district(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where the research will be performed (company labs, collaborating academic sites) and ensure site capabilities match proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protections and IRB Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether human subjects are involved, provide IRB approval dates and Human Subject Assurance numbers, and explain exemptions if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for protection of human subjects, consent processes, and necessary IRB documentation or pending review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: IACUC, Animal Welfare and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe use of vertebrate animals, IACUC approval status, animal welfare assurance, details of animal models, procedures (anesthesia, blood collection), euthanasia methods, and humane endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document that experiments will follow institutional IACUC protocols and AVMA euthanasia guidelines; provide justification of species, numbers, husbandry and oversight arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSL / Select Agent Compliance and Facility Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: For work with high-risk agents (e.g., H5N1), specify biosafety containment level (BSL-3/3E), facility certification by CDC/APHIS, Select Agent registration, and personnel training/security risk assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the certified facility, staff training completion, security assessments, and that the investigator is listed on Select Agent registration where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Analysis and Sample Size Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide statistical design: specify significance level (alpha = 0.05), desired power (80%), effect size assumptions, planned statistical tests (two-tailed unpaired Student t test, ANOVA), and sample size calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how animal numbers were chosen to balance minimizing animal use and achieving statistical significance; reference prior data for variance/effect size assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunogenicity and Efficacy Assay Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe immunological assays to be used (e.g., ELISA for serum IgG/IgA, in vitro micro-neutralization assay, ELISPOT for IFN-γ), sample collection (serum, lavage), and in vitro/in vivo challenge testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give assay references, standard operating procedures, number of replicates/groups, and where assays will be performed (e.g., micro-neutralization at TechnoVax, animal work at Baylor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Controls, Comparators and Adjuvant Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to include appropriate controls (e.g., inactivated virus vaccines) and consider combinations with adjuvants or standard vaccines if novel constructs are insufficient alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe control groups and contingency plans to test adjuvants or prime-boost strategies if immune responses are suboptimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Problems and Alternative Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly discuss potential technical problems (e.g., improper folding of remodeled HAs) and alternative approaches (e.g., structural modeling, testing additional HA subtypes, combining constructs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific mitigation strategies and collaborators (e.g., structural biologist) to address foreseeable experimental failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide project timelines and an Activities & Milestones chart showing when aims and major tasks will be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use milestones to demonstrate feasibility within the proposed period and to support future Phase II plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan / Data Sharing and IP Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: State intent for sharing data with NIH and via peer-reviewed publications but note that protection of patentable information will be established prior to disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for data/material sharing, timelines for release, and how intellectual property will be protected before public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full references for cited literature supporting background, rationale, methods and precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key primary literature and authoritative resources (e.g., WHO, CDC, BMBL) that support the scientific approach and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual Agreements and Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters of support and consortium/subaward agreements that document collaborations, access to facilities (e.g., Baylor BSL-3) and shared resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach formal letters outlining commitments, roles, and resource/access provisions; include subaward budgets where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist and Certifications (Inventions, Program Income, Disclosure Permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398 checklist, answer questions about inventions and patents, program income, and provide disclosure permission statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose prior inventions/patents as required, indicate anticipated program income, and state whether the Government can disclose applicant contact info if no award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Analysis Computing Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe availability of computing and statistical software (e.g., SAS, STATVIEW, EXPO) and servers to perform data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List software and data analysis plans to show capability for statistical evaluation and data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Numbers and Ethical Endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: State total number of animals proposed, group sizes per aim, and define clinical criteria for humane euthanasia (e.g., rapid shallow respiration, >20% weight loss).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit humane endpoint criteria, explain monitoring plans, and justify total animal numbers relative to statistical design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / Section 508 Conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Note accessibility and reformatting for Section 508 conformance; provide contact info for accessibility issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submitted documents are accessible to users with disabilities and include alternative text or reformatted materials when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and FOIA Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that FOIA requests for applications and summary statements may be subject to exemptions and redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark confidential material appropriately and understand that NIH will redact sensitive information when responding to FOIA requests.
